questions.stem: A technician needs to check a hard drive's file system for errors AND scan for bad sectors, recovering any readable data from them. Which command?
questions.explanation: chkdsk /r scans for bad sectors and recovers readable data from them. It also implies /f (fix file system errors).
questions.trap: chkdsk /f only fixes file-system errors; it does NOT scan for bad sectors.

questions.stem: A tech suspects malware and wants to see which Windows executable is responsible for each open network connection. Which command (and what prompt does it need)?
questions.explanation: netstat -b maps each open connection to the executable (binary) that owns it. It requires an elevated prompt.
questions.trap: netstat -a shows ALL connections including listening ports but does not name the owning program.

questions.stem: An admin edits a Group Policy at the domain controller. A user is logged in on a workstation and the new setting hasn't taken effect. Which command applies the policy immediately without forcing a logout?
questions.explanation: gpupdate forces a group policy refresh and applies the new settings immediately on the workstation.
questions.trap: gpresult only REPORTS which policies are applied; it does not pull new ones.

questions.stem: Which Windows command-line tool is described as the robust file copy that handles huge files and automatically retries when the network drops?
questions.explanation: robocopy ('robust copy') is the right tool for large transfers across unreliable links; it can resume and retry.
questions.trap: rsync is the Linux/Unix equivalent; on Windows you reach for robocopy.

questions.stem: A corporate web app times out intermittently. Other internal sites work fine. Which command BEST identifies where in the network path the slowdown happens?
questions.explanation: pathping combines ping and tracert to test the connection quality at every hop along the path, exposing which hop is slow or dropping packets.
questions.trap: ping confirms reachability but does not tell you WHERE on the path the problem is.

questions.stem: Which command shows the workstation's MAC address and DNS servers along with the IP configuration?
questions.explanation: ipconfig /all expands the basic ipconfig output with MAC address, DNS servers, DHCP info, and more.
questions.trap: Plain ipconfig shows IP, subnet, and gateway only - no MAC, no DNS server list.

questions.stem: After a suspected malware cleanup, a tech wants to verify that critical Windows system files are intact and repair any that are corrupted. Which command?
questions.explanation: sfc /scannow (System File Checker) scans protected system files and repairs damaged ones - the right tool for OS file corruption.
questions.trap: chkdsk verifies the file system on a drive, not the integrity of Windows OS files.

questions.stem: A user calls to ask why they can't run an admin tool from the command line. As the tech, you want a one-line command to confirm which user account is currently logged in at the prompt. Which command?
questions.explanation: whoami prints the currently logged-on user, which is the fastest way to confirm what permissions the prompt is running under.
questions.trap: hostname returns the computer name, not the user.

questions.stem: A web server's IP address has changed. From a Windows workstation, which command is built to query a DNS server for the new address by hostname?
questions.explanation: nslookup is the dedicated DNS query tool. It asks a DNS server for the IP behind a given name.
questions.trap: ping will also resolve a name to an IP as a side effect, but nslookup is the right tool for the job.

questions.stem: Which Windows command-line utility is described as the powerful tool for creating or deleting partitions on a drive from the command line?
questions.explanation: diskpart is the advanced Windows partition utility for creating, deleting, and managing partitions from the command line.
questions.trap: format only prepares an existing partition's file system; it does not create or delete partitions.
